subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the exact final set of 14 third-party action revisions be approved for workflows that use secrets, write tokens, security uploads, and release credentials?
rationale: Green static checks cannot establish the trustworthiness or operational compatibility of newly selected third-party executable revisions, and repository ownership explicitly routes several touched workflows to security review.

options.title: Audit and approve final pins
options.body: Verify every digest against its intended upstream release, complete the direct Codex contract check, review privileged workflow changes, and approve only the unchanged final head.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate Codex, app-token, Docker publishing, and CodeQL revisions into smaller PRs if the grouped security and behavior audit cannot be completed confidently.

options.title: Defer until the branch stabilizes
options.body: Leave the existing pins in place and recreate or refresh the update after Dependabot access and repeated rebasing stop changing the reviewed head.

recommendation.title: Audit and approve final pins
recommendation.body: Verify every digest against its intended upstream release, complete the direct Codex contract check, review privileged workflow changes, and approve only the unchanged final head.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history spans action-runtime modernization, docs-agent ownership, Docker workflow maintenance, and current PR awareness, making them the best individual routing candidate alongside the security-operations reviewers.
